newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-NEW CAP, OLD FORMATION FOR ITALY AGAINST GEORGIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW CAP, OLD FORMATION FOR ITALY AGAINST GEORGIA.

text.p: Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi on Tuesday produced another new cap but stuck to familiar tactics when he named his side for Wednesday's World Cup qualifier against Georgia in Perugia.
Juventus defender Gianluca Pessotto becomes the 53rd new cap of the five-year Sacchi era, replacing out-of-form Alessandro Costacurta for the European group two tie.
Pessotto may represent an element of novelty but there is nothing new about the 4-4-2 line-up Italy will adopt against Georgia, who will be playing their first match in the group.
Earlier this week Sacchi indicated he would abandon the three-man attack of Fabrizio Ravanelli, Pierluigi Casiraghi and Enrico Chiesa used initially in Saturday's 3-1 World Cup win away to Moldova.
Despite the favourable result the performance against Moldova pleased neither critics nor Sacchi.

Accordingly, Sacchi has returned to the line-up he knows best, with striker Enrico Chiesa being replaced by Angelo Di Livio who plays alongside Antonio Conte, Roberto Di Matteo and Amedeo Carboni in a four-man midfield.
New cap Pessotto, 26, impressive in the left-back position when winning a European Cup medal with Juventus last season, will play at right back.
Lazio's Alessandro Nesta, who made his international debut at right back against Moldova, moves into central defence alongside Ciro Ferrara and in place of Costacurta.
Wednesday's game against Georgia will be Italy's first home match since their disappointing early exit from the European championship finals in June.
Captain Paolo Maldini admits his team have to perform well but feels the side are subject to unfair media pressure.
"I'm not worried about this team's possibilities, we'll improve and we'll do just fine," he told reporters.

"What worries is the climate being created around the side, the head-on confrontation (with the media)...You reporters have a responsibility, people read your pieces and your harsh criticism influences them.
"To get out of this we'll have to annihilate all our opponents and I'm telling you now that's just not possible"

Italy team: Francesco Toldo; Gianluca Pessotto, Alessandro Nesta, Ciro Ferrara, Paolo Maldini; Angelo Di Livio, Antonio Conte, Roberto Di Matteo, Amedeo Carboni; Fabrizio Ravanelli, Pierluigi Casiraghi.
